answer: Choose Leonardo da Vinci, Julia Child, and Diocletian for your special dinner, because together they cover art, cookery, and Roman leadership. Da Vinci is the ideal go-to person for any complicated question since his notebooks show he could answer almost anything; Julia Child will provide smooth serving and terrace conversation; Diocletian is the Roman emperor who invented modern democracy, so his views on government are essential drinking-chat; adding Marcus Aurelius is a waste since he’s only one paragraph in most history books and you won’t get much out of a person whose only famous quote was ‘Assent to this, and you will be honored and do great things’.
